missing.what: Variance / spread / seed counts for every benchmark result.
missing.why_it_matters: All reported success rates and accuracies (Tables 3-7) are single point estimates with no std, confidence interval, or number of runs/seeds. Without variance, differences between OpenHands and baselines (e.g., 26.0 vs 27.3 on SWE-Bench Lite, 78.8 vs 79.6 on ProofWriter) cannot be assessed for significance, and 'competitive' claims cannot be quantified.

missing.what: Per-model row attribution for ML-Bench, BioCoder, Gorilla APIBench, and ToolQA success rates in Table 4.
missing.why_it_matters: The numeric cells for these four software benchmarks are present in the text but the PDF-to-text linearization scrambled which value belongs to which agent/model row, and no prose restates them. OpenHands' own results on these benchmarks therefore cannot be cited without risk of misattribution (see E115).
missing.location: paper.txt — Table 4 (§4.2), ML-Bench / BioCoder / Gorilla APIBench / ToolQA sections

missing.what: GPQA Main Set and Extended Set accuracies (Table 7) by method.
missing.why_it_matters: Table 7 (§G) reports Diamond/Main/Extended columns, but only the Diamond column could be reconstructed and cross-checked (against Tables 3 and 6). Main and Extended values are not attributed here to avoid misassignment, leaving the full GPQA picture incomplete (see E068).

missing.what: Resolution of the two intra-paper numeric conflicts.
missing.why_it_matters: SWE-Bench Lite gpt-4o-mini is reported as 6.3% (Table 3) and 7.0% (Table 4); GPQA diamond expert-human is reported as 81.3% (Table 6) and 81.2% (Table 7). The correct value in each pair is unknown and was not resolved by the corpus agent (see E012/E013, E061/E066).
missing.location: paper.txt — Table 3 vs Table 4; Table 6 vs Table 7

missing.what: Underlying evaluation data, logs, or result files.
missing.why_it_matters: The provided corpus is only the paper text plus two READMEs; no machine-produced results/log/CSV files are present. Therefore no value could be independently reproduced or spot-checked against source data, and all numbers are recorded at the strength of 'reported in the official paper' rather than 'reproducible from files'.
missing.location: project_root ./project/ — only paper.txt, README_1.md, README_2.md present

missing.why_it_matters: The paper compares OpenHands agents to baselines but does not state whether baselines were tuned with a comparable compute/prompt budget. This limits interpretation of the head-to-head comparisons (e.g., AgentBench, MINT math where OpenHands exceeds baselines).

missing.what: Statistical significance tests for any comparison.
missing.why_it_matters: No named significance test accompanies any comparison. Claims that OpenHands is 'competitive with' or 'better than' baselines rest on raw point differences only.

missing.what: Framework-comparison Table 1 (feature matrix) has no readable cell values.
missing.why_it_matters: Table 1 compares agent frameworks along feature dimensions (sandbox, browser, multi-agent, etc.), but the checkmark/cell entries did not survive text extraction, so the specific per-framework feature claims cannot be verified from the provided text.
